text: Pattern: permit_surge. Riverfront keeps absorbing the big filings: P-2026-01011 cleared plan review in three weeks, fast for this cycle. When the review queue moves that quickly, groundbreaking tends to follow within a month, and it did. The drainage desk in East Industrial is still the bottleneck; anything routed there adds a month before you see movement. Data gaps: none today; permits, inspections, and zoning feeds all current.

Pattern: permit_surge. Split week: P-2026-00990 passed foundation on the first attempt while P-2026-00975 failed framing a second time, and repeat framing failures usually mean a contractor problem, not a paperwork problem. Watch reinspection dates over press releases; the inspection log tells you which projects are actually moving. Data gaps: zoning calendar was one day stale this run; hearing items may lag.

Pattern: permit_surge. The lesson from prior filing waves: a surge in filings is not a surge in construction until plan review clears. P-2026-00788 is the cautionary row, six weeks parked at drainage review while its announcement made the rounds. Count issued permits, not filed ones, before calling a boom. Data gaps: none today; all three feeds current.

Pattern: seasonal_slowdown. Quiet weeks are where stalls hide. P-2026-00801 has been in review with no examiner assigned, and nobody notices until the renewal deadline forces it. On slow weeks the useful work is auditing the in-review pile for projects going quietly dead. Data gaps: inspections feed missing this run; movement calls rest on permit status alone.
